items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters, and PC Gamer counts 91 story missions in total.
Push Square and Insider Gaming put the story at 93 missions across five chapters, so counts differ depending on whether optional missions are included.

The chapter titles are Just Like Paradise, Paradise Lost, Tits Ass Drug Money, Vice City Baby, and Top of the World Ma. Chapter 1 is set in the Leonida Keys and Chapter 2 in Port Gellhorn. Chapters 3 and 4 are set in Vice City, and Chapter 5 is the shortest at 7 missions.
You play as the duo Jason and Lucia. The story follows their journey through Leonida, and Jason is the only playable character in Chapter 1.
Supporting characters include Brian (Jason's boss), Donnie, Cal, Moses (an auto-shop owner who buys stolen cars), and Randy (a high-end car fence who appears in Chapter 3).
Leonida has six main regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park. Each is modeled on a different part of Florida.
The map is also divided into five counties: Vice-Dale, Leonard, Kelly, Lummox and Mariana.
Collectible cards come in 18 sets, and you can sell them at pawn shops. You can also view your collection in a wooden box in your apartment.
Cards are scattered across all 5 counties, in public places, in homes, in stores you can rob, and during missions. Collecting three cards in each county unlocks the card achievement.
Races take place at 40 unique locations. Entering costs an entry fee and a vehicle rental fee, but a win pays more than you put in.

Side content includes hunting missions for Bret in Lummox County, with Chapter 2 unlocking them for Jason only. It also includes demolition derbies at Ambrosia Raceway, which pay roughly $3,800 to $6,300 per win.
As Jason, you can scuba dive for sunken treasure around Key Lento for Kenton. Finding all the treasure at each dive spot eventually pays out tens of thousands of dollars.
Moses starts buying stolen cars in Chapter 2, paying roughly $1,000 to $5,000 each for cars with no tracker. Randy's wish list has 18 high-end sports cars worth $30,000 or more apiece.
Gang hideouts respawn their loot and can pay $10,000 to $30,000 per run, which makes them a strong late-game money source. The big vault always comes back.
Bank vault robberies unlock near the end of Chapter 4 and can pay up to $200,000. They instantly give you a 4-star wanted level.
Banks and loan stores need a dye pack jammer, which you get from a character in Chapter 3, so wait until then. With the snap gun you can enter stores through back doors without triggering the alarm.
Buses and trains give you a cheap way to fast travel on a schedule, since RydeMe is expensive early on. You cannot replay missions once you finish them.

Ultimate Edition vehicles include the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak at Jason's house from Chapter 1, and a '67 Dominator Buggy in your Paradise garage from Chapter 2. The Shitzu Squalo appears in Chapter 4, and the '95 Grotti Cheetah in Chapter 5.
Many PS5 players report crash error CE-108255-1, some during the Pipework mission and some at the prologue, and no fix has been confirmed.
A glitch that uncaps the frame rate has been reported on version 01.002.001 with an Xbox Series X and a 120Hz display. The game is otherwise locked to 30 FPS, and the glitch may get patched.
The game has no dedicated first-person mode at launch. A glitch can force first-person view, and you have to reload your save to get back to third person.
